e: Borrowed from Japanese 合気道家 (aikidōka).
From Middle English [Term?], from Old Norse aka (“to drive, sail, navigate”), from Proto-Germanic *akaną.

Borrowed from Japanese 合(あい)気(き)道(どう) (aikidō, “aikido”, literally “way of adapting the spirit”), from 合(あい) (ai, “together, unify”) + 気(き) (ki, “spirit; breath”) + 道(どう) (dō, “way”). Doublet of hapkido.
Borrowed from Fanagalo aikona, haikona. Compare Xhosa hayi, kona, Zulu hhayi no.
From Aikin + -ite, after Arthur Aikin (1773-1854), English geologist.
